_howTo: The six driver cards on the home page, in order. figure.basis is reported, estimated or pending; a pending figure renders as an em dash marked pending, never a guess. status is one of lobby-holding, in-play, on-paper, in-court, reform-moving, pending.

drivers.label: Section 6001
drivers.title: The physician-owned hospital ban

figure.source: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, Pub. L. 111-148, section 6001 (2010)

drivers.text: The year Congress froze physician-owned hospitals in place. No new ones. No expansion of the ones that survived.

drivers.label: Price Transparency
drivers.title: Prices you can see but cannot use

figure.source: 45 CFR Part 180, Hospital Price Transparency, effective January 1, 2021

drivers.text: Hospitals have been required to publish prices since January 2021. Almost none of it is usable to shop for care.

drivers.label: Certificate of Need
drivers.title: Permission to compete, granted by your competitors

figure.source: Rojas Report CON desk, 35 jurisdictions (34 states and the District of Columbia), data/overview.json

drivers.text: And the District still require a state board's approval to open or expand a facility, with incumbents allowed to object.

drivers.label: Hospital Subsidies
drivers.title: Tax exemption, the 340B program, DSH and provider taxes
drivers.text: A year in public money flowing to the same systems that lobby to keep competitors out.

drivers.label: CMS Favoritism
drivers.title: Same service, higher price, if a hospital owns the building
drivers.text: What Medicare pays a hospital outpatient department over an independent office for the same infusion or scan.

drivers.label: Stark & Anti-Kickback
drivers.title: The rules that keep physicians from building rivals

figure.source: Ethics in Patient Referrals Act (Stark I), Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1989, Pub. L. 101-239

drivers.text: Written to stop self-referral. Now the reason independent physicians cannot integrate the way health systems already do.
